newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures range-bound in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures range-bound in choppy trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures bounced about in a 30 cent range in choppy, but light trade on Wednesday, seeming content to settle mid-range, brokers said.
"There is just not a lot happening here," a broker said. "No one wants to be caught pushing things too much."
Jan Brent was trading up 20 cents at $22.94 a barrel at 1605 GMT, off its intraday high of $23.02.
Dec gas oil followed a similar range-bound pattern, trading up 50 cents at $217.50 a tonne, below a high of $218.25.
Generally positive fundamentals, including cold weather and largely bullish stock figures, bolstered prices, brokers said.
But they said the looming Iraqi re-entry into the market continued to overhang things. Some analysts said the market may not yet have fully factored in the increased production.
"The full psychological effect of an Iraqi re-entry is not in the market," said Charles Gray, analyst at Prudential-Bache in London.
Brokers said they expected thin trade Thursday and Friday, when NYMEX will be closed because of the Thanksgiving holiday.
In its latest weekly report, the Energy Information Agency (EIA) reported inventory levels largely in line with Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute (API) figures.
Crude oil stocks (excluding Strategic Petroleum Reserves) fell 4.8 million barrels to 300.2 million, while distillate stocks climbed 1.3 million to 114.5.
The API reported slightly smaller changes, albeit in the same direction. However, it reported a fall in heating stocks in the crucial East Coast market by over a million barrels.
"The figures were largely supportive," a broker said.

Iraq announced at the biannual OPEC meeting in Vienna, which kicked off on Wednesday, that it would resume oil exports "within a matter of weeks" and that it expected to export between 700,000 and 800,000 barrels per day.
